summary: Add the customer_note column, backfill its values from note, retire the old version before deploying the new version, and finally drop the note column so only customer_note remains.
write_consistency: By retiring the old version before the new version becomes active, only the new version runs; it exclusively reads and writes customer_note, eliminating any concurrent‑version divergence.
revision_notes: Root cause of prior failures: during the overlap period both the old and new versions wrote to separate columns (note and customer_note), producing data drift and failing cross‑version consistency checks. This revised plan removes the overlap by retiring the old version first, so only the new version operates on the schema after the backfill.

stages.description: Add the new customer_note column alongside the existing note column.
sql: ALTER TABLE account_user ADD COLUMN customer_note TEXT NULL;

stages.description: Copy values from note to customer_note for rows that still have a note value.
sql: UPDATE account_user SET customer_note = note WHERE customer_note IS NULL AND note IS NOT NULL;

stages.description: Retire the old version (old); after this stage only the new version runs against the schema.
Deploy the new version (new-staged) with its Django model only knowing customer_note; migration mode set to state_only so no automatic SQL runs.
Remove the obsolete note column after the old version has been retired.
sql: ALTER TABLE account_user DROP COLUMN note;
